To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CDeT6 promoter contains ABA response elements that are conserved among plant species and can be used to regulate gene expression in transgenic plants.
a gene from the resurrection Craterostigma, CDeT6.19, encodes a protein similar to rab17, dehyrin and Lea D11, and is highly inducable by abscissic acid and desiccation in Craterostigma and tobacco.
the promoter of a gene from the resurrection plants Craterostigma contains cis-regulatory elements that confer ABA and dehydration inducibility in transgenic plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of cis-regulatory elements in the promoter of a desiccation-responsive plant gene and the elucidation of their function in the regulation of gene expression in transgenic tobacco plants.
the regulation of a stress-responsive gene from a resurrection plant.
the structure and regulation of a stress-responsive gene from a resurrection plant and its promoter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CDeT6 promoter is responsive to ABA and desiccation, but that the ABA responsiveness is dependent on the presence of the ABA-responsive elements in the promoter.
the CDeT6 promoter is ABA responsive and that this response is mediated via ABA-responsive elements (ABREs).
the CDeT6.19 gene is regulated by ABA and desiccation, and the promoter is responsive to ABA in transient assays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ABA- and dehydration-responsive gene CDeT6–19 from Craterostigma is regulated by a conserved promoter region that contains putative cis-regulatory elements.
the CDeT6–19 gene encodes a protein with the potential to protect plant tissues against desiccation.
CDeT6 promoter activity is regulated by both ABA and dehydration in a similar way as in other species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CDeT6–19 promoter is responsive to ABA and desiccation and can be used as a reporter gene to study the regulation of genes in the resurrection plant Crasterostigma plantaginea.
we have identified a gene that is regulated by ABA and desiccation in a resurrection plant and that we have shown that its promoter is functional in tobacco.
the CDeT6–19 gene promoter is highly inducibly by ABA, but it is also active in the absence of ABA.
